bull.b: The 44-gigawatt backlog and scheduled deliveries through 2030 provide substantial revenue visibility and support production planning. This contracted base reduces reliance on immediate spot-market demand, helps underpin capacity expansion, and gives the company a durable foundation for future cash generation.

Very high gross and adjusted EBITDA margins demonstrate strong current earnings power, particularly with the benefit of a higher U.S.-produced module mix. Sustained profitability can fund technology development, manufacturing expansion, and other strategic investments without requiring heavy financial leverage.

Extremely low leverage and solid returns on equity give First Solar meaningful financial flexibility. The company can continue investing in capacity and technology while retaining greater resilience against operating volatility, because its earnings are not dependent on substantial borrowing.

bear.b: Reduced volume, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA guidance indicates that near-term growth is facing execution and demand pressure despite the long backlog. Lower current-year throughput can delay cash realization, weaken operating leverage, and make future earnings more dependent on successful capacity ramps.

Recent cash generation has lagged reported earnings materially, with operating cash flow covering less than half of net income and free cash flow falling sharply. If this pattern persists, it could constrain internally funded expansion and make reported profitability less representative of available financial resources.

Unresolved FEOC rules and changing Section 232 tariff conditions complicate customer procurement decisions and pricing. This uncertainty can delay bookings, disrupt international and domestic volume planning, and reduce visibility into the economics of future contracts even when structural U.S. demand remains favorable.
